exclusions.reason: Cover, title, author date and addressed-draft identification are provenance, not substantive error candidates. Delivery is unverified.
Overall approval, list of requested amendments and high-protection priorities are normative; substantive premises are inventoried at their developed passages.

Proposed statutory training safeguards, accessible alternatives and dialogical requirements are recommendations. Conditional digital capabilities and practical limitations are assessed separately; no realised savings or superiority is inferred.

Four-year maximum and ABAS guidance are proposals. Data minimisation and preferred authentication architecture are policy choices; historical ASGA publication and general effectiveness assertions remain unresolved.

Preferred PPE wording, rest periods and sanction clarity are recommendations; current hierarchy and definitions separately checked. Incidental mistaken subsection citation in government rationale is not promoted into author error.

Proposed mobile equivalence, interface duties, database architecture and privacy safeguards are policy/legal drafting recommendations. Predicted responsibility transfer and service savings are not observed effects.

ABAS assessment, deletion of ambiguous terms and possible future occupational exclusions are proposed risk controls or forecasts. Actual current scope and conditional scientific mechanism are separately assessed.
Portal accessibility, interoperability, free access, exception route and preferred legal formulation are recommendations, not claims that existing portals necessarily fail.

Suggested transition periods, revised nomenclature, costing programme and dates for future evaluation are normative. Quantified draft assumptions and limited cost completeness separately checked; no forecast is converted into a factual error.

Minor typographic and citation-cleanup list is incidental; material annex, medium/form and legal-instrument distinctions are captured elsewhere. Conclusion restates preferences, not independent claims.
Bibliography, self-description and contact information are incidental. Bibliographic availability does not establish the cited proposition or historical draft identity.
